<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3df181b20b29dc67b2f77c4c80cb1068b5c55a23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c5a5d51901f69e7e5047295faab4e2ad5902da12`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts + content/docs/ai/agents.mdx
Security-touching: no

First record on PR #38031 for card #38012 (the follow-up to N1 and N2 of record 7222359751 on PR #38003). Read: the card body and its three comments (triage 7223000822, claim 7224432682, dev report 7224881775); the PR title, body, its 3-file list and its comments (docs-drift 7224891493, head comment 7225468412, review claim 7225491125); the net diff against the merge base `8b47659e` (+16/-4); the 70 check-runs on the head (60 success, 10 skipped, none failed). Nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run; git objects were read in place.

`Security-touching: no`. The words this PR adds teach a compile-time refusal and a fact about the conversion chain. The `knowledge` row's sentence about retrieval scoping is `main`'s text, unchanged by the hunk. The seat decides the label.

### ① Derived judgments

- `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`: one hunk, 2 lines for 6, wholly inside the block comment at :98-110. No schema, type, export or accept set changes. Right.
- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`: two table rows, one clause added to each (the `tools` row and the `knowledge` row at :311-312). Docs prose; no other cell or sentence moves. Right.
- `.changeset/38012-agent-knowledge-absorbed-conversion-note.md`: new. Right, see ②.
- The file surface the claim declared (the docblock, the two rows, one changeset) is the whole diff.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch: right. The package's `files` list publishes `src/**/*.zod.ts` (`packages/spec/package.json:261`), so the comment is published bytes, and a comment is a patch. The docs page belongs to no package and needs no entry. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

Clause-②: no. Correct on the PR body and in the changeset: no accept set moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

The changeset, sentence by sentence against the tree:
- "the note where `AIKnowledgeSchema` used to live no longer says the protocol-17 `agent-knowledge-topics-to-sources` conversion is still in the chain": true, the hunk.
- "That rename was absorbed before release into the removal of the whole `agent.knowledge` block": true, by the ABSORBED note at `conversions/entries/17/sharing-rule-access-level-full-to-edit.ts:17-24`.
- "no registry or entry module carries the id": true. Across the head the id appears in four places only: this changeset, the rewritten docblock, the ABSORBED note, and the comment at `conversions/entries/18/connector-resilience-keys-removed.ts:31` that cites it as a precedent. All four are prose; no `id:` line carries it.
- "`retired-after.census.json` has no row for it": true. The census has no occurrence of the id (its only `agent-knowledge` rows are `agent-knowledge-removed`).
- "Comment only: no schema, type or export changes": true, see ①.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7224881775: `open_questions` empty; `security_findings` none; `out_of_scope_findings` empty.
- Dev narrowing, three gates not measured locally (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`): answered by the head's check-runs, none failed.
- The dev's one probe (TS2353 for `tools` and for `knowledge`, a clean control literal, against the rebuilt spec dist) is the dev's evidence, not a committed test. It is not re-run here; ④ reaches the same result from the types.
- The card marked the docs half-clause optional ("if it does not read well in the table, leave it out"). It was added; it reads cleanly in both rows.
- Docs-drift comment 7224891493 reports no anchor for `agent.zod.ts`: expected for a comment-only hunk; the page that documents these keys is in this diff.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`**, the rewritten sentence at :104-109, clause by clause against the head:
- "No conversion for the block's old `topics` spelling is in the chain": true. No entry module under `conversions/` and no registry line declares the id or any other `topics` rewrite for `agent.knowledge`.
- "the protocol-17 `agent-knowledge-topics-to-sources` rename was absorbed before release into the removal of the whole block": true to the cited note, which says the rename "lived inside the same unreleased major that now REMOVES the whole `agent.knowledge` block" and was "Folded pre-release".
- "(the ABSORBED note in `conversions/entries/17/sharing-rule-access-level-full-to-edit.ts`)": the file exists at that path under `packages/spec/src/` and the note is at :16-24.
- "so no registry or entry module carries that id and `retired-after.census.json` has no row for it": true, as under ②.
- The four sentences above it in the docblock are PR #38003's text, unchanged, and were judged true in record 7222359751.
- The hunk is inside a block comment; no code line moves. `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Test Core` are green on the head.

Tried to break it: the new sentence could be read as saying a removal conversion is still in the chain. It does not say so. It says the rename was absorbed into the removal, which is the history the cited note records, and it makes no claim about where the removal entry lives today.

**`content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`**, the added clause in each row, "the key is not on the type, so a `defineAgent({ … })` literal that sets it fails `tsc` as an excess property, and the strict schema refuses it at parse as an unknown key":
- `defineAgent` (`agent.zod.ts:649`) is not generic. Its one parameter is typed as the `z.input` of `AgentSchema` directly, so an object literal passed inline is a fresh literal checked against that exact type; nothing widens it first.
- `AgentSchema` (:345) is `lazySchema` over `strictObject`. `lazySchema` (`shared/lazy-schema.ts:34`) returns its factory's type unchanged. `strictObject` (`shared/strict-object.ts:541`) returns `closedObject(z.object(shape, …).strict())`, and `closedObject` returns its argument's type unchanged. The input type is therefore a closed object type with no index signature and no catchall. The spread `MetadataProtectionFields` adds the one named key `_lock`.
- The shape declares neither `tools` nor `knowledge`. `lifecycle` and `memory.longTerm.store` are the keys still held as `retiredKey()` members; these two are not. So the literal fails on the excess-property rule (TS2353), which is what the rows say, and the rows do not claim the old by-name `never` refusal.
- The clause is scoped to "a `defineAgent({ … })` literal", which is exactly where the check applies. A value arriving through a variable, a spread or JSON is not claimed, and the parse refusal the row keeps covers those.
- "the strict schema refuses it at parse as an unknown key, naming the upgrade guide": true for both keys (`agent.test.ts:101-114` and `:232-242`). The added words "at parse" are accurate.
- Each row's removal line, why-sentence and replacement are `main`'s text, unchanged.

Observation, outside the diff and not graded: the ABSORBED note the docblock cites says "(`agent-knowledge-removed` below)", and on the head no entry module under `packages/spec/src` declares that id either; it survives only in that comment and in the census rows. The sentence this PR writes does not depend on it. Read, not reviewed; a follow-up card if the owning area wants the note tidied.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
